title.title: The Correspondence of Esther Roberts Hunt Collins

msIdentifier.institution: Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College

projectDesc.p: The correspondence of Quaker minister Esther Roberts Hunt Collins is stored at the Friends Historical Library of Swarthmore College. With the generous support of H. David and Joyce E. Hunt, Library staff scanned and transcribed these letters in 2024 and encoded the text in TEI.

div.p: These few lines may inform thee that I received thy acceptable letter sent by the hands of our dear Friends from your parts who were at Baltimore—at which place we were favored to meet, & many precious opportunities we had at that Yearly Meeting. Diverse others, valuable Friends attended there. And Oh, I was favored at times to behold my poor unworthy condition with earnest desires to be what I ought to be in a greater degree, feeling great need to be more deep and weighty in spirit to fit me to stand in my allotment with propriety. Dear Brother, I take thy hint kindly in regard to taking heed not to be lifted up. Oh, there is need for us to watch & pray & that continually lest we enter into temptation. Yet I think the more we experience of favor the more it reduces self & inasmuch as we have an unwearied enemy envying our happiness, what great need of a good lookout. May both thee & me labor to keep to the watch tower.

I feel a desire that each of us may experience a growing in the root of religion. As to myself I feel so encompassed with frailties & infirmities that there is a fear indeed in my heart lest I shall be a stumbling block in the way.

There is also great cause of humble acknowledgment on my part, of the wonderful kindness of our Blessed Lord, who hath dealt bountifully with me even to admiration, may a humbling sense thereof impress my heart with gratitude to him for his benefits which are manyfold of a truth.

I remembered thy love to Reece Cad.—with letting him know it would be acceptable to thee to receive some account of his Indian expedition. His reply was that he was not so ready a scribe as those want, & he thought it was a most time for thee to come & see us or to that purport.
I am not able at present to give thee any very clear account of Brother Robert, but from accounts that are lately received expect he is on the road moving out.

As thou desired to know what was like to take me from home, may inform it was appointments from our meetings, the first on a request of Sweekly Friends for the establishment of their meeting. Also, Sandy Creek & Sandy Hill have requested the establishment of their meetings, as likewise the privilege of holding preparative meetings (& further being to attend the Yearly Meeting at Baltimore which took me three weeks from home at that time) these being all weighty matters & I, a poor unskillful creature. It has been trying, truly the harvest is great and faithful qualified laborers few.

closer.salute: May we unite, in servant breathings of soul for a increase thereof, is the desire of thy affectionate Sister,

postscript.p: my love to Friends & relations, thy wife & children, particularly with thyself, farewell
